results.snippet:
The French capital has hundreds of direct flights that connect it with most countries on all continents. If you travel from Europe, France’s central location makes it very easy to reach by train or bus.

    Within the country, you’ll find a robust network of high-speed trains that makes it easy to reach other student cities such as Lyon, Toulouse or Bordeaux.

    Bon voyage!

### Typical duration

Masters in France mostly take between 1 year and 2 years to complete.

### Typical tuition fees

At public universities, students from the EU/EEA pay either €243 or €601 per year, and other international students pay €3,770. At private universities and business schools, fees are higher, up to around €25,000 per year.

Ready to study in France?

Find the right Master’s degree now [...] Students who are citizens of the EU, EEA, Switzerland or Andorra pay tuition fees of €243 per year (not quite for free but almost) at universities and usually €601 at schools of Engineering (but there might be different fees - make sure to ask).
    International students from other countries pay tuition fees of €3,770 per year for their Masters.

   At private institutions and especially at many of France’s well-renowned business schools the Masters tuition fees will be higher, up to around €25,000 per year.
4. ### Find out how to apply 💡

   The application process for Master’s degrees in France depends on a few main factors: your nationality, your current country of residence, and which type of institution(s) you want to apply to.

   For public universities, it works like this: [...] To apply for a Master’s degree in France, you typically need to prepare the following documents:

    Undergraduate degree certificate (for degrees obtained outside France, a translation into French might be required)
    Proof of English skills (such as IELTS or TOEFL score certificates)
    A detailed curriculum vitae / résumé
    A personal statement describing your personal and career goals
    References or letters of recommendation
    For non-EU students: a copy of their photo ID/passport, or a copy of the residency permit (carte de séjour), or a confirmation of receipt of the residency permit application for the current year
    Overview of personal work (portfolio, bibliography, thesis, research project, etc.)
    Questionnaire by the university
